blocks.text: Leaderless databases (Dynamo, Cassandra, Riak, ScyllaDB) let any replica accept reads and writes. With no leader to order operations, they rely on a set of primitives: quorums to bound staleness, sloppy quorums and hinted handoff to stay available, version vectors to detect conflicts, read repair and Merkle-tree anti-entropy to converge, and gossip to track who's alive. Interviewers expect you to name and explain these when you design a key-value store.

Because any 2 of 3 replicas overlap with any other 2 of 3, a quorum read always includes at least one replica with the latest acknowledged write. The coordinator returns the newest version and **read-repairs** the stale replica in the background.

items.title: Owner down
items.text: Key k belongs to replicas A, B, C; C is unreachable.

items.title: Write elsewhere
items.text: Coordinator writes to A, B and stand-in D, tagging D's copy with a hint: "belongs to C".

items.title: Handoff
items.text: When gossip reports C is back, D streams the hinted writes to C and deletes them.

items.title: Trade-off
items.text: Writes stay available, but a quorum read of A, B, C during the outage might miss data that lives on D.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Claiming R + W > N guarantees strong consistency. With sloppy quorums, concurrent writes and last-write-wins clocks, it doesn't. It bounds staleness in the normal case.

v1 = {A:1}           written via A
v2 = {A:1, B:1}      read v1, written via B      → v2 descends from v1
v3 = {A:2}           read v1, written via A      → v2 and v3 are CONCURRENT → keep both

Read repair only fixes keys that get read. To fix everything else, replicas periodically compare **Merkle trees**: each leaf hashes a small key range, each parent hashes its children. Two replicas compare roots; if equal, they're in sync. If not, they descend only into the differing branches, so finding the few divergent ranges among billions of keys takes a logarithmic number of comparisons, and only those ranges are streamed.

items: Every second, each node picks a few random peers and exchanges its view of cluster membership (node, status, heartbeat counter, version).
News spreads like an epidemic: everyone knows within O(log N) rounds, with no central coordinator to fail.
**Phi-accrual failure detection:** instead of a fixed timeout, compute how unusual the current silence is given past heartbeat intervals, and suspect a node when φ crosses a threshold.
Gossip also spreads schema versions and token (ring) ownership in Cassandra.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Membership is gossiped, writes use sloppy quorums with hinted handoff, reads use quorum plus read repair, and Merkle-tree anti-entropy converges everything in the background.

items: A **lease** is ownership with an expiry ("leader until 12:00:30"), renewed by heartbeats. It lets a leader act without asking a quorum each time.
Leases assume bounded clock drift and can't stop a paused process from acting after expiry.
**Fencing tokens** close the gap: each new lease gets a higher number, and storage rejects writes with stale tokens.
